hints: Focus on drawing out the full displayed structure, so you can see every double bond and every oxygen clearly.
Count one pi bond for each double bond present, and count two lone pairs on each oxygen atom in the carboxylic acid group.
Remember that tetrahedral $sp^3$ carbon atoms in $\text{CH}_3$ groups make a molecule non-planar, even if the $C=C$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ parts are flat.
walkthrough:
**Draw the structure fully**

Let's expand tiglic acid to see all the bonds. It is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{OH}$.

This shows one $C=C$ alkene bond and one $C=O$ carbonyl bond in the acid group.

**Check statement 1 for pi bonds**

Remember, every double bond contains one sigma bond plus one pi bond.

$$ \text{number of } \pi \text{ bonds} = 1 \text{ (from C=C)} + 1 \text{ (from C=O)} = 2 $$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 for lone pairs**

Only oxygen has lone pairs here. Each oxygen has 2 lone pairs to complete its octet.

$$ \text{lone pairs} = 2 \text{ (on C=O oxygen)} + 2 \text{ (on O-H oxygen)} = 4 $$
So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 for planarity**

The $C=C$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ parts are planar, but the two $\text{CH}_3$ groups contain $sp^3$ tetrahedral carbon.

Tetrahedral carbons have H atoms above and below the plane, so not all atoms can be in the same plane. So statement 3 is incorrect.

Therefore only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes statement 3. While 1 and 2 are true, the methyl $\text{CH}_3$ carbons are tetrahedral ($sp^3$), so their hydrogens stick out of the plane.
options.B: Correct because only 1 and 2 are true. There are two pi bonds (one in $C=C$, one in $C=O$) and four lone pairs (two on each oxygen of $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$). Statement 3 is false due to tetrahedral methyl groups.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes statement 3 and omits statement 1. Statement 1 is definitely true (two double bonds give two pi bonds), and statement 3 is false because of the 3D shape of $\text{CH}_3$ groups.
options.D: Incorrect because it omits statement 2. Statement 2 is true since the carboxylic acid group has two oxygens, each with two lone pairs, giving four in total.
